title: Agentic-Priors: Using Large Language Models to Address the Cold Start Problem in Preference Elicitation
title_zh: Agentic-Priors：利用大型语言模型解决偏好收集中的冷启动问题

paragraphs.en: An agent that learns a user’s preferences from their choices faces a cold start problem: before any choices are observed, it must rely solely on a prior. Informative priors are usually fitted to historical choice data, which new tasks and deployments lack. To address this, we present Agentic-Priors, which lets agentic systems use the implicit knowledge of large language models (LLMs) instead. Specifically, an LLM states a new user’s trade-offs in interpretable terms, such as willingness to pay or value of time, which we map to a prior over multinomial logit coefficients. This prior is then refined by a Bayesian learner as choices are observed. Across seven choice datasets, Agentic-Priors improves cold start accuracy over an uninformed prior by 5–40 percentage points. It also outperforms AutoElicit, a state-of-the-art LLM prior-elicitation method, on three datasets and loses on one. It is up to 18 points more accurate than in-context learning, and never significantly worse. Against hierarchical Bayes models fitted to surveys of increasing size, our approach is worth roughly 6–40 surveyed users, in terms of log-loss, so its value is concentrated in a deployment’s first users.

paragraphs.en: For an agent to make personalised recommendations, or even autonomous decisions, it must estimate a user’s preferences. A standard approach observes the user’s choices and updates a utility model by Bayesian inference ( Chajewska et al., 2000 ; Boutilier, 2002 ) . Before the first choice, however, the agent can rely only on its prior, and a poor prior means poor early recommendations and slower learning. This is known as the cold start problem.
paragraphs.zh: 为了让智能体能够提供个性化推荐，甚至做出自主决策，它必须估计用户的偏好。 一种标准方法是观察用户的选择，并通过贝叶斯推断更新效用模型（Chajewska et al., 2000；Boutilier, 2002）。 然而，在用户做出第一次选择之前，智能体只能依赖其先验，而糟糕的先验意味着糟糕的早期推荐和更慢的学习。 这就是所谓的冷启动问题。

paragraphs.en: The usual remedy is population data. A hierarchical Bayes model (HBM) fitted to other users’ choices on the same task gives an informative prior ( Allenby and Rossi, 1998 ) , and conditioning it on user characteristics makes that prior user-specific ( Campigotto et al., 2017 ) . But this needs a choice dataset for the task at hand, which a new product, service or deployment does not have. Without one, the agent falls back on an uninformed prior, which says nothing about what the user prefers.
paragraphs.zh: 常见的补救办法是群体数据。 用层级贝叶斯模型（HBM）拟合其他用户在同一任务上的选择，可以得到一个有信息量的先验（Allenby and Rossi, 1998），而以用户特征为条件对其进行调整，可使该先验具有用户特异性（Campigotto et al., 2017）。 但这需要针对当前任务的选择数据集，而新产品、新服务或新部署并不具备这样的数据集。 缺少这样的数据时，智能体只能退回到无信息先验，而它对用户的偏好没有任何说明。

paragraphs.en: Large language models (LLMs) encode broad knowledge about how people make choices ( Argyle et al., 2023 ; Goli and Singh, 2024 ) , which suggests a third option: using this implicit knowledge to derive more informative priors. Specifically, in our approach, an LLM reasons about how a user would trade off the attributes of a choice, and states those trade-offs in a form a choice model can use. This can then be used to provide relevant recommendations or make autonomous actions on the user’s behalf. Here, the difficulty is that utility coefficients have no natural units ( Train, 2009 ) , so an LLM has nothing to anchor their magnitude to. We instead ask for trade-offs on a reference scale it can reason about, such as how much the user would pay to save an hour of travel, and convert these into coefficients.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）编码了关于人们如何做出选择的广泛知识（Argyle et al., 2023; Goli and Singh, 2024），这提示了第三种选项：利用这种隐式知识来推导更具信息量的先验。 具体而言，在我们的方法中，LLM 会推理用户将如何在选择的各个属性之间进行权衡，并以选择模型可以使用的形式表述这些权衡。 这随后可用于提供相关推荐，或代表用户执行自主行动。 这里的难点在于，效用系数没有天然的量纲（Train, 2009），因此 LLM 没有可以锚定其数值大小的参照。 我们转而要求 LLM 给出它能够推理的参照尺度上的权衡，例如用户愿意为节省一小时的出行时间支付多少钱，然后把这些权衡转换为系数。

paragraphs.en: Against this background, we introduce Agentic-Priors , which elicits a user-specific prior from a single LLM call. The LLM is given a description of the choice task and, optionally, whatever is known about the user, such as their demographics or other relevant context (e.g. the purpose of a trip). Agentic-Priors requires no historical choice data, and then hands the prior to a Bayesian learner that updates it as real choices arrive (Figure 1 ), e.g. when a user chooses from a set of presented options. We evaluate it on seven stated- and revealed-choice datasets from transport, vehicle purchase, consumer goods and finance, against an uninformed prior, an LLM that predicts choices directly using in-context learning ( Brown et al., 2020 ) , and AutoElicit ( Capstick et al., 2025 ) , a state-of-the-art approach that uses LLMs as priors for general machine learning problems. We also compare our approach to HBM ( Allenby and Rossi, 1998 ; Rossi and Allenby, 2003 ) , which is widely used in choice modelling when detailed historical population data is available.
paragraphs.zh: 在此背景下，我们提出 Agentic-Priors，它通过单次大语言模型调用引导出用户特定的先验。 大语言模型会获得关于选择任务的描述，以及（可选的）有关用户的已知信息，例如其人口统计特征或其他相关背景（如出行目的）。 Agentic-Priors 无需历史选择数据，随后将该先验交给一个贝叶斯学习器，随着真实选择的到来（例如用户从一组呈现的选项中进行选择）对其进行更新（图 1）。 我们在来自交通、车辆购置、消费品和金融领域的七个陈述性及揭示性选择数据集上对其进行评估，对比对象包括无信息先验、使用上下文学习（Brown et al., 2020）直接预测选择的大语言模型，以及 AutoElicit（Capstick et al., 2025）——一种将大语言模型作为通用机器学习问题先验的最先进方法。 我们还将本方法与 HBM（Allenby and Rossi, 1998；Rossi and Allenby, 2003）进行比较，该模型在选择建模领域被广泛使用，但前提是能够获得详细的历史人口数据。

paragraphs.en: Agentic-Priors improves cold start accuracy over an uninformed prior on all seven datasets, by 5 to 40 percentage points. In accuracy, it outperforms AutoElicit on three datasets, loses on one and is inconclusive on the remaining three. Predicting choices directly with the LLM, with past choices given in context, is never significantly better than eliciting a prior and updating it, and is up to 18 percentage points less accurate. To measure what the prior is worth in data, we compare it with HBMs fitted to surveys of increasing size: in log-loss it is worth between about six and about forty surveyed users, depending on the dataset, and in accuracy at most about six on all datasets but one. Its value is therefore real but confined to a deployment’s first users. Moreover, on most datasets a prior elicited from the task description alone, without any information about the user, is worth almost as much: the value lies mainly in the LLM’s knowledge of the task.

paragraphs.en: An agent that recommends or decides on a user’s behalf must estimate their preferences from few interactions—the cold start problem of recommender systems ( Schein et al., 2002 ) . Research on preference elicitation has largely optimised which comparisons to present: decision-theoretic formulations select queries that reduce utility uncertainty or minimax regret ( Chajewska et al., 2000 ; Boutilier, 2002 ; Braziunas and Boutilier, 2007 ; Zintgraf et al., 2018 ) , and adaptive conjoint and efficient choice designs pursue the same goal through experimental design ( Toubia et al., 2004 ; Sauré and Vielma, 2019 ; Rose and Bliemer, 2009 ) . Every such method, however, proceeds from what the agent already believes before the first question is asked—and that belief alone determines its behaviour while no choices have yet been observed. In contrast, we here study the complementary lever: the user-specific information available before any interaction.

paragraphs.en: Random-utility models make that belief explicit and interpretable, representing a user’s preferences as a coefficient vector over attribute trade-offs ( McFadden and Train, 2000 ; Train, 2009 ) . Conventionally, the distribution over those coefficients is estimated from a population of earlier users, with mixed logit and hierarchical Bayes capturing how preferences vary across individuals ( Allenby and Rossi, 1998 ) . Closest to our setting, FAVOUR maps sociodemographic profiles to population-informed priors for personalised routing and then refines them by Bayesian learning ( Campigotto et al., 2017 ) . This pipeline is similar to ours, but differs in where the prior comes from. Recent personalisation methods likewise learn shared preference structure from prior users before adapting to a new one ( Poddar et al., 2024 ; Shenfeld et al., 2025 ; Bose et al., 2026 ) . All provide informative starting points, but all require a historical choice dataset from comparable users performing a comparable task—assumptions we make explicit in Section 3.3 , and whose cost motivates this work.

paragraphs.en: LLMs offer a different source for the same object. One line of work elicits priors for Bayesian models directly from an LLM and examines how well its stated uncertainty is calibrated ( Capstick et al., 2025 ; Renda et al., 2026 ) , though the elicited prior is one per task rather than one per user, and the work considers general machine learning tasks rather than choice models; hence, we adapt this approach to choice data, with and without user conditioning, as baselines. A second line of work simulates users or augments human choice data, including individual-level mimicry conditioned on socio-economic microdata, with mixed evidence on behavioural fidelity ( Argyle et al., 2023 ; Bisbee et al., 2024 ; Goli and Singh, 2024 ; Wang et al., 2026 ; Kinzinger and Hartmann, 2026 ) ; these yield simulated answers rather than a distribution over preference coefficients. LLMs given stated preferences are also competitive recommenders near cold start ( Sanner et al., 2023 ) , but return recommendations, not a model of trade-offs. A third line places LLM knowledge inside sequential decision loops: CBLI warm-starts bandits with synthetic preferences and subsequent work identifies negative transfer when those preferences are misaligned ( Alamdari et al., 2024 ; Bayley et al., 2026 ) , while OPEN combines LLMs with Bayesian experimental design to select informative queries ( Handa et al., 2024 ) . There the knowledge enters as synthetic training data for a black-box reward model, not as a prior over interpretable coefficients.

paragraphs.en: The LLM receives two messages via a single prompt. paragraphs.en: Our primary elicitor is Qwen3-32B (4-bit AWQ, reasoning disabled), chosen because it is open-weight, relatively small and cheap to run, so a prior can be elicited for every new user without a proprietary API. To test sensitivity to this choice, we repeat cold start elicitation on three datasets covering both reference scales (Swissmetro, Cars and Bank) with seven open-weight models from four families (Mistral, Qwen, Gemma, Llama; 8–31B) on a public API, with identical prompts and no per-model tuning (full results in Appendix D ). Cold start accuracy is largely insensitive to the elicitor: on Swissmetro, every model except Gemma-3-12B is within 2 2 percentage points of our primary model (none significant), and on Cars and Bank the others differ by at most 4 4 points in either direction. Log-loss is more sensitive, since it also penalises miscalibrated magnitudes: on Swissmetro, only Mistral-Small-24B matches our primary model, the other 24–31B models are 0.03 0.03 – 0.06 0.06 worse, and Llama-3.1-8B is 0.10 0.10 worse. The exception on both metrics is the previous-generation Gemma-3-12B, which states implausibly large monetary values, loses 5 5 – 6 6 accuracy points on Swissmetro and Cars, and is worse than an uninformed prior in log-loss on both; Gemma-4 does not show this failure.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的主要引导模型是 Qwen3-32B（4-bit AWQ，关闭推理功能），选择它的原因是它是开放权重的，规模相对较小且运行成本低，因此无需专有 API 即可为每位新用户引导出先验。 为检验对该选择的敏感性，我们在三个覆盖两种参照尺度的数据集（Swissmetro、Cars 和 Bank）上，用来自四个家族（Mistral、Qwen、Gemma、Llama；8–31B）的七个开放权重模型，通过公共 API 并使用完全相同的提示词、不进行任何针对单一模型的调优，重复冷启动引导实验（完整结果见附录 D）。 冷启动准确率对引导模型的选择基本不敏感：在 Swissmetro 上，除 Gemma-3-12B 外的所有模型与我们的主要模型相差不超过 2 2 个百分点（均不显著）；在 Cars 和 Bank 上，其他模型在任一方向上的差异至多为 4 4 个百分点。 对数损失更为敏感，因为它还会惩罚校准不当的幅度：在 Swissmetro 上，只有 Mistral-Small-24B 与我们的主要模型相当，其他 24–31B 模型差 0.03 0.03 – 0.06 0.06，而 Llama-3.1-8B 差 0.10 0.10。 在两个指标上都是例外的是上一代的 Gemma-3-12B，它给出的货币金额大得不合理，在 Swissmetro 和 Cars 上损失 5 5 – 6 6 个准确率百分点，并且在两个数据集上的对数损失都差于无信息先验；Gemma-4 没有出现这种失败。

sents.en: Cold start accuracy is largely insensitive to the elicitor: on Swissmetro, every model except Gemma-3-12B is within 2 2 percentage points of our primary model (none significant), and on Cars and Bank the others differ by at most 4 4 points in either direction.
sents.zh: 冷启动准确率对引导模型的选择基本不敏感：在 Swissmetro 上，除 Gemma-3-12B 外的所有模型与我们的主要模型相差不超过 2 2 个百分点（均不显著）；在 Cars 和 Bank 上，其他模型在任一方向上的差异至多为 4 4 个百分点。

sents.en: Log-loss is more sensitive, since it also penalises miscalibrated magnitudes: on Swissmetro, only Mistral-Small-24B matches our primary model, the other 24–31B models are 0.03 0.03 – 0.06 0.06 worse, and Llama-3.1-8B is 0.10 0.10 worse.
sents.zh: 对数损失更为敏感，因为它还会惩罚校准不当的幅度：在 Swissmetro 上，只有 Mistral-Small-24B 与我们的主要模型相当，其他 24–31B 模型差 0.03 0.03 – 0.06 0.06，而 Llama-3.1-8B 差 0.10 0.10。

sents.en: The exception on both metrics is the previous-generation Gemma-3-12B, which states implausibly large monetary values, loses 5 5 – 6 6 accuracy points on Swissmetro and Cars, and is worse than an uninformed prior in log-loss on both; Gemma-4 does not show this failure.

paragraphs.en: AutoElicit ( Capstick et al., 2025 ) is the closest existing LLM-based prior elicitation method. We run the authors’ code, adapting only the prompt template: AutoElicit targets linear and logistic regression, so the template for choice tasks is ours, with role paraphrases generated by the authors’ rephrasing prompt. The same LLM as for our method is prompted with every combination of 10 10 paraphrased system roles and 10 10 user roles ( S = 100 S=100 elicitations, temperature 0.1 0.1 ), each time stating a Normal mean and standard deviation for each parameter. Following the authors, the prior is the diagonal Gaussian that moment-matches the equal-weight mixture of the S S elicited Normals, common to all users. As in their implementation, intercepts are not elicited but receive a fixed 𝒩 ⁡ ( 0 , 1 ) \mathcal{N}(0,1) prior on the unnormalised dummy scale. AutoElicit + z i z_{i} adds z i z_{i} to every user-role prompt and moment-matches per user; since the intercepts keep their fixed prior, z i z_{i} affects only the attribute coefficients.
paragraphs.zh: AutoElicit（Capstick et al., 2025）是目前最接近的基于大语言模型的先验收集方法。 我们运行原作者的代码，仅对提示模板进行调整：AutoElicit 针对的是线性回归和逻辑回归，因此选择任务所用的模板由我们提供，其中的角色改写由原作者的改写提示生成。 使用与我们方法相同的 LLM，对 10 个改写的系统角色与 10 个用户角色的每一种组合进行提示（S=100 次收集，温度为 0.1），每次为每个参数陈述一个正态分布的均值和标准差。 遵循原作者的做法，先验为对角高斯分布，通过对 S 个收集到的正态分布进行等权混合并做矩匹配得到，且对所有用户相同。 在他们的实现中，截距不进行收集，而是在未归一化的虚拟变量尺度上赋予固定的 𝒩(0,1) 先验。 AutoElicit + z_i 在每个用户角色提示中加入 z_i，并对每个用户分别进行矩匹配；由于截距保持其固定先验，z_i 仅影响属性系数。

paragraphs.en: To test whether a prior and a choice model are needed at all, the same LLM predicts choices directly. For user i i , the prompt contains z i z_{i} , the T T choices observed so far (the same ones the Bayesian learner sees) and the held-out tasks, and the LLM returns a probability for each alternative: learning happens only in context. We use our method’s system prompt and decoding settings (one call per user and value of T T ), score the same held-out tasks, and mix 10 − 3 10^{-3} of uniform probability into each prediction so that a confidently wrong answer has finite log-loss.
paragraphs.zh: 为了检验先验和选择模型是否真的必要，我们让同一个大语言模型直接预测选择。 对于用户 i i，提示词中包含 z i z_{i}、迄今为止观察到的 T T 个选择（与贝叶斯学习者所见的相同）以及留出任务，大语言模型为每个备选项返回一个概率：学习仅发生在上下文中。 我们使用本方法所用的系统提示词与解码设置（每个用户的每个 T T 取值调用一次），对相同的留出任务进行评分，并在每个预测中混入 10 − 3 10^{-3} 的均匀概率，使得自信但错误的答案具有有限的对数损失。

paragraphs.en: We address three questions. First, at cold start ( T = 0 T=0 ), is a prior elicited by Agentic-Priors more accurate than the alternatives that need no historical data (Section 6.1 )? Second, does its advantage persist as the user’s choices are observed, and is updating an explicit prior better than giving the LLM those choices in context (Section 6.2 )? Third, how much population data is the prior worth (Section 6.3 )? Unless otherwise stated, all comparisons are paired over the same 100 test users per dataset, and “significant” means p < 0.05 p<0.05 in a paired t t -test, Holm-corrected within dataset (Appendix B ).

paragraphs.en: Table 3 shows results at T = 0 T=0 . Agentic-Priors + z i z_{i} is significantly more accurate than the uninformed prior on all datasets, by 5 to 40 percentage points. In accuracy, it beats AutoElicit on LPMC, EV and Beer and loses only on Swissmetro; adding z i z_{i} to AutoElicit changes no accuracy verdict in its favour. In-Context Learning is less accurate on six datasets, significantly on LPMC and Bank, and never significantly better. Both HBMs remain ahead, except on Beer, where Agentic-Priors + z i z_{i} is level with the HBM without z i z_{i} (no significant difference) using no data. Among methods that need no historical data, Agentic-Priors + z i z_{i} is thus the most consistent at cold start: always more accurate than the uninformed prior, never significantly behind In-Context Learning, and behind AutoElicit only on Swissmetro. Swapping covariances between Agentic-Priors + z i z_{i} and the HBM shows that its remaining gap to the HBM at cold start lies in the prior’s mean: with the HBM’s covariance, our prior’s accuracy changes by at most 2 points on every dataset. The LLM’s stated trade-offs, not the spread placed around them, are what population data improves on (Appendix E ).

paragraphs.en: Figure 3 shows performance as the user’s choices are observed. paragraphs.en: We introduced Agentic-Priors, in which an LLM states a user’s trade-offs on a reference scale, such as willingness to pay, that we map to a prior over choice-model coefficients. Across seven datasets, the prior is more accurate than an uninformed prior at cold start on every dataset, beats AutoElicit in accuracy on three, and outperforms in-context learning with the same information. Its value is real but bounded: in log-loss it is worth between about 6 and 40 surveyed users, and most of it comes from the LLM’s knowledge of the task rather than of the individual. An LLM prior is therefore best seen as a way to start learning before any data exist, not a substitute for population data once a small survey is available.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 Agentic-Priors，其中一个 LLM 阐明用户在某个参考尺度上的权衡，例如支付意愿，我们将其映射为对选择模型系数的先验。 在七个数据集上，该先验在每个数据集的冷启动场景下都比无信息先验更准确，在三个数据集上准确率超过 AutoElicit，并且在信息相同的情况下优于上下文学习。 它的价值是真实但有界的：以对数损失衡量，其价值约相当于 6 到 40 名受访用户，且其中大部分来自 LLM 对任务的知识，而非对个体的知识。 因此，LLM 先验最好被视为一种在任何数据存在之前就开始学习的方法，而不是在已有小型调查数据时对人群数据的替代。

paragraphs.en: Future work should extend the LLM’s role beyond the prior: an LLM-assisted learner could choose which choices to ask about or revise the prior when observed choices contradict it, while keeping the Bayesian update that in-context learning lacks. paragraphs.en: Covariance swap (Table 10 ). Each prior is split into its mean and its covariance, and the two halves are exchanged between Agentic-Priors and the HBM. At T = 0 T=0 , exchanging covariances barely moves either prior: with the HBM’s covariance, our prior’s accuracy changes by at most 2 points on every dataset, and the HBM with our covariance stays within about 1 point of the HBM. The cold start gap therefore lies in the prior’s mean. Once choices are observed, learning speed follows the covariance: with the HBM’s covariance, our mean gains more from the observed choices on every dataset but Swissmetro, and after the last step all users reach it is within about 1 point of the HBM’s accuracy on LPMC, Cars CN, Beer and Bank. Conversely, the HBM’s mean with our isotropic covariance learns more slowly than the HBM on most datasets.

paragraphs.en: What a small survey adds (Table 11 ). Our mean is combined with the covariance of an HBM fitted on N N surveyed users and compared with that HBM, using the exchange-rate surveys of Section 6.3 . In log-loss, our mean is better only for the smallest surveys (EV at N = 10 N=10 , Beer up to N = 15 N=15 ); from 25 users the survey’s own mean is as good or better on every dataset, and in accuracy it is better at every N N on six datasets. sents.en: For each dataset, we fit HBM + z i z_{i} (as in the benchmark of Section 5.3 , with the same prompt-matched user characteristics and settings) to random surveys of N N users drawn from the non-test users, and score each fit at T = 0 T=0 on the same test users, task permutations and posterior-draw seeds as our prior.
sents.zh: 对于每个数据集，我们将 HBM + z i z_{i}（如第 5.3 节基准测试中那样，使用相同的提示匹配用户特征和设置）拟合到从非测试用户中随机抽取的 N N 名用户的调查数据上，并在与我们的先验相同的测试用户、任务排列和后验采样种子下，以 T = 0 T=0 对每次拟合进行评分。

paragraphs.en: Exchange rate. For each N N , the paired difference between the HBM and our prior is averaged over users and survey draws. N ∗ N^{*} is where a non-decreasing least-squares fit of this difference, against log ⁡ N \log N , crosses zero (interpolated in log ⁡ N \log N ); its 95% interval comes from 2,000 bootstrap resamples of the test users. When the HBM is already ahead at the smallest fittable survey, only a bound is reported. In Figure 4 , each N N ’s band combines the user and survey-draw uncertainty of that N N ; HBMs fitted on the smallest surveys can be badly over-confident, which is why our prior can be worth a few users even where it is worse than the uninformed prior (Cars CN, log-loss).
paragraphs.zh: 汇率。 对于每个 N N，HBM 与我们的先验之间的配对差异会在用户和调查抽样上取平均。 N ∗ N^{*} 是该差异对 log N \log N 的非递减最小二乘拟合穿过零点的位置（在 log N \log N 中插值）；其 95% 区间来自对测试用户的 2,000 次自助重抽样。 当 HBM 在最小的可拟合调查上已经领先时，只报告一个界限。 在图 4 中，每个 N N 的置信带合并了该 N N 的用户不确定性和调查抽样不确定性；在最小调查上拟合的 HBM 可能严重过度自信，这就是为什么即使我们的先验在效果上不如无信息先验（Cars CN，对数损失），它仍可能相当于几名用户的价值。
